patches.old: This is why PTSD symptoms can return under stress (spontaneous recovery) or in new contexts (renewal).
patches.new: This is why an extinguished fear can come back by three distinct routes, which the exam keeps apart: **spontaneous recovery**, the return of the response after a delay with nothing new happening; **renewal**, its return when the cue is met in a context different from the one where extinction took place; and **reinstatement**, its return after re-exposure to the aversive event itself or to a comparable stressor. Note that spontaneous recovery is defined by the passage of time alone, not by stress.

patches.old: - Recognition (in adults) that the fear is excessive.
patches.new: - Fear that is out of proportion to the actual threat. Note that the DSM-5 dropped the DSM-IV requirement that adults recognise their own fear as excessive or unreasonable; that judgement is now the clinician's, because many patients genuinely believe the danger is real.

sources.title: Haaker, Golkar, Hermans & Lonsdorf, “A review on human reinstatement studies”, Learning & Memory (2014) — defines return of fear by the passage of time (spontaneous recovery), a change of context (renewal) and re-exposure to the aversive event (reinstatement)

Kraynak & Hart, summary of DSM-5 anxiety disorder criteria changes — specific phobia and social anxiety disorder no longer require the individual to recognise the fear as excessive; the judgement now rests with the clinician

visual.title: How an extinguished fear comes back
visual.alt: A flow from acquisition through extinction to two competing memories, then three cards distinguishing spontaneous recovery triggered by time, renewal triggered by a change of place and reinstatement triggered by the aversive event recurring; a panel showing amygdala overactivity, ventromedial prefrontal underactivity and reduced hippocampal volume in PTSD with the low-cortisol contrast against depression; and a three-question triage for the diagnoses.
visual.caption: Extinction never deletes the original fear memory, so the three returns are expected rather than evidence that the therapy failed.
